text:
priya: thinking of converting the search-indexer from a Deployment -> StatefulSet because each replica needs a stable DNS name + its own PVC. planning to do this via terraform (kubernetes_manifest). looking for a rollout + terraform checklist — any gotchas? want minimal downtime and no data loss.

matt: 👍 good call if you need stable identity + per-pod storage. checklist: PVC reclaim policy, volumeClaimTemplates, updateStrategy partitioning, pdb, readiness gating, and terraform lifecycle rules. i can paste snippets.

priya: yes please — also worried about HPA + statefulsets. we currently have an HPA on the deployment.

matt: HPA doesn't work the same with StatefulSet replicas (it can if you manage replicas via the apps/v1 scale subresource, but it's brittle). recommended options: either keep manual/cron scaling, move scaling logic to a controller that understands StatefulSets, or use an external scaler that updates the StatefulSet.spec.replicas. for immediate migration, remove HPA first so we don't get conflicting controllers.

olivia: quick infra note: ensure PVC reclaimPolicy is Retain or snapshot before change. if you use Delete, PV can be removed when PV object gets deleted. snapshot before switching to be safe. also double-check storageclass volumeBindingMode for cross-node scheduling.

matt: Terraform tips: if using kubernetes_manifest or helm_release, mark volumeClaimTemplates in lifecycle.ignore_changes so TF doesn't try to rewrite existing PVCs. also run a dry-run, then apply with small partitioned rollout. example terraform snippet:```hcl
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "search_statefulset" {
  manifest = yamldecode(file("./manifests/search-statefulset.yaml"))
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = ["manifest.spec.template.metadata.annotations", "manifest.spec.volumeClaimTemplates"]
  }
}
```

priya: example YAML for the updateStrategy + pdb + readiness?

matt: sure — small example (keep partition so you can roll one at a time):```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: search-indexer
spec:
  replicas: 3
  serviceName: search-indexer
  podManagementPolicy: Parallel
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 1    # set to highest ordinal you want to keep old, then lower to roll
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: search-indexer
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: indexer
        image: ghcr.io/redwood/indexer:stable
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health/ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/drain-graceful"]
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 100Gi
```

matt: PodDisruptionBudget example:```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: pdb-search-indexer
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: search-indexer
```

olivia: extra notes:
- make sure readiness probe blocks termination until indexer has finished leadership handoff (so we don't get split-brain).
- if you set podManagementPolicy: Parallel, scaling up is faster but startup ordering is not guaranteed — choose OrderedReady if startup ordering matters.
- snapshot PVCs first; schedule snapshot in backup system if possible.

priya: good call on readiness + preStop. what's best practice for partition planning during cutover?

matt: do a staged cutover:
- set StatefulSet.spec.replicas to same number as existing deployment
- start with partition = replicas (which means no pods are updated)
- create resources in k8s (apply manifests) so PVs are created as pv/pvc bindings if needed
- lower partition to replicas-1 to update highest ordinal only, verify index + metrics, then proceed one ordinal at a time
- update partition -> 0 when ready for full rollout
This gives full control.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: terraform plan ✅, dry-run applied to staging ✅, snapshots created: snap-2025-01-21-search-1 ✅

priya: thanks — one more: secrets handling. we store DB creds in k8s secret via sealed-secrets. should that change?

olivia: keep using sealed-secrets or ExternalSecrets. make sure the new manifest references the same secret name and kube namespace. avoid recreating secrets during tf apply (use lifecycle ignore_changes or import existing secret into TF state).

matt: also: add an annotation to template.metadata.annotations with a rollout timestamp on every desired update so you can force pod recreation without changing other fields. example: "rollout.redwood.com/ts: \"2025-01-21T15:00:00Z\""

priya: perfect. i'll do snapshots + import secrets into tf state, apply to staging with partitioned rollout, and post results. thanks all :heart_exclamation:
